sa29:1.2: One time, the Buddha was staying at Anāthapiṇḍada’s Park in Jeta’s Grove of Śrāvastī.
sa29:2.1: There was then a certain monk named Samṛddhi who came to visit the Buddha.
sa29:2.2: He bowed his head at the Buddha’s feet, withdrew to stand to one side, and said to the Buddha,
sa29:2.3: “The Bhagavān says ‘the teaching of a Dharma teacher.’
sa29:2.4: What’s called the teaching of a Dharma teacher?”
sa29:3.1: The Buddha said to the monk,
sa29:3.2: “[Good, good!] Do you want now to know the meaning of ‘the teaching of a Dharma teacher’?”
sa29:4.1: The monk said to the Buddha,
sa29:5.2: “[Listen closely!] Listen closely, and consider it well.
sa29:5.3: I will explain this for you.
sa29:5.4: If a monk teaches disillusionment with form, being free of desire for it, and completely ceasing it, this is called the teaching of a Dharma teacher.
sa29:5.5: It’s the same with feeling, conception, volition, and awareness … teaches disillusionment with awareness, being free of desire for it, and completely ceasing it.
sa29:5.6: This is called the teaching of a Dharma teacher.”
sa29:6.1: When that monk heard what the Buddha taught, he celebrated and rejoiced.
sa29:8.1: [31] Well versed, [32] the well taught Dharma,
sa29:8.4: “What is the teaching of a Dharma teacher.”
